title: Iraqi basics
about: The most common words of spoken Iraqi Arabic that are not Standard Arabic: counted in 3.7 million words that Iraqis wrote in comments and messages, most common first, 50 to a unit. It builds on the Arabic basics course: words you already know from Standard Arabic, even said a little differently (گال for قال, چبير for كبير), are left out, and the grammar course teaches the patterns. Every meaning is backed by a published source, mostly Wiktionary. Each word has one short everyday sentence as people say it in Baghdad, with vowel marks and its English translation; ⟦ ⟧ marks the part that translates the word. گ is the Iraqi g (Standard ق) and چ is ch (often Standard ك). A note under a word says how it differs from a Standard Arabic word that looks the same.
